METEO 1N: Extreme weather brings immense economic costs and threatens individuals, communities, and ecosystems.

METEO 5: Non-technical introduction to the physical processes important in the formation of various severe and unusual weather phenomena.
METEO 6N: In HIST 6N / METEO 6N, we'll survey how weather and history are integrated throughout time.
METEO 7: This course provides an overview of factors that serve as the basis for understanding climate change and climate variability.
METEO 51N: This course examines the inter-relationship between what we know and what we see, through an introductory exploration of art and science.

METEO 133N: Climate change is not only a political, economic, and social crisis, it presents one of the great moral problems of our time.

METEO 215: Forecast methods/data discussed prior to nightly weather forecast entry.

METEO 273: Algorithm design and implementation for meteorological analysis and forecasting.

METEO 332N: This interdomain course introduces students to the science and policy of greenhouse gas emissions.

METEO 414: A survey of conceptual models and analysis techniques for mesoscale atmospheric features.
METEO 415: Modern techniques in weather analysis and forecasting.
METEO 416: Competitive, simulated, operational, real-time forecasting is covered.
METEO 419: Issues relating to the prediction and dispersion of air pollutants are discussed.

METEO 422: Survey of advanced dynamical topics including instabilities, numerical modeling, and others of current interest.
METEO 426: METEO 426 will provide students with a practical understanding of the structure of numerical weather prediction (NWP) models in the context of their application to real world precipitation forecasting.
METEO 431: Classical thermodynamics applied to both the dry and the moist atmosphere.
METEO 434: In METEO 434, students will learn the basic operating principles and applications of weather radar, a primary observing platform for both operational and research meteorologists.

METEO 454: Physical processes and their measurement in the lowest layers of the atmosphere; application to hydrology, plant systems, and air pollution.
METEO 455: The basic principles of atmospheric flow, introduction to the modeling of turbulent diffusion, and the use of EPA dispersion models.

METEO 465: A topical survey of physical, chemical, and dynamical processes at work in the stratosphere and mesosphere (middle atmosphere).
METEO 466: A survey of planetary atmospheres and the chemical and physical processes by which they form and evolve.
METEO 469: Examination of global warming and climate change: the basic science, projects, impacts, and approaches to mitigation.
METEO 470: The fundamental principles that govern Earth's climate and their relevance to past and future climate change.

METEO 473: Application of statistical and numerical methods to practical problems in meteorology.
